previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: The patient was admitted for evaluation of persistent chest pressure and shortness of breath, initially noted after his primary care physician identified ST elevations on a prior EKG. He underwent cardiac catheterization, which revealed in-stent restenosis of the OM1 artery, successfully treated with a drug-eluting stent. His symptoms resolved post-procedure. During admission, he was also diagnosed with an infected tooth (#21), for which he was started on antibiotics, pain medication, and a chlorhexidine mouth rinse, with plans for outpatient extraction. He remained on anticoagulation for prior pulmonary embolism, bridged with Lovenox post-procedure. His diabetes, hypertension, and heart failure were managed throughout. He was discharged home with a walker, new medications including Plavix, and close follow-up instructions.

radiology_notes.text:
INDICATION:  chest pain and EKG changes.  concern for pneumonia or CHF.

FINDINGS: Mediastinal, hilar, and cardiac contours are unremarkable.  Low lung
volumes are noted bilaterally with no focal opacification concerning for
pneumonia.  No pleural effusion or pneumothorax.  No soft tissue or osseous
abnormalities.

IMPRESSION:  No acute process.

INDICATION:  ___ man with history of coronary artery disease and
saddle pulmonary embolism who presents with worsening shortness of breath on
exertion.  Assess for progression of pulmonary embolism.

COMPARISON:  CTA chest ___.

TECHNIQUE:  MDCT-acquired images were obtained from the thoracic inlet through
the upper abdomen prior to and after the administration of 100 cc of Optiray
intravenous contrast.  Coronal, sagittal, and right and left oblique
reformatted images were also displayed.

FINDINGS:  The pulmonary arteries demonstrate no filling defects.  The
previously seen extensive pulmonary emboli have resolved since the prior
study. Heart size is normal without pericardial effusion.  Coronary artery
stents are again seen.

Nonspecific ground glass opacities are noted at the lung bases. While this may
reflect atelectasis, NSIP could also have this appearance. The lungs are
otherwise clear.

The airways are patent to the segmental level.  There is no pleural effusion. 
Small mediastinal and hilar lymph nodes do not meet CT criteria for pathologic
enlargement.  There is no axillary lymphadenopathy.

This examination is not tailored for subdiaphragmatic evaluation.  Visualized
aspects of the upper abdomen demonstrate a mildly distended gallbladder.

BONE WINDOWS:  No concerning osseous lesions are identified.

IMPRESSION:  
1.  No pulmonary embolism.  Resolution of previously seen pulmonary emboli.

2.  Nonspecific ground glass opacities at the lung bases which may reflect
atelectasis. However, NSIP could have this appearance. If clinically
indicated, HRCT is recommended for further evaluation.
